articles.title: Jimmy Kimmel on Trump’s joke about Iran bombing LA: ‘Our own president wishing death to America’
articles.summary: Late-night hosts discuss Trump’s rally line that Iran should bomb LA or San Diego as he continues to defend costly war
articles.body:
Late-night hosts reacted to Donald Trump 's inflammatory comments about Iran bombing US cities as he continues to defend his war in the region.

As the US president's approval ratings get lower, Jimmy Kimmel noted on Tuesday evening, something curious happens: "somehow his engine fills up with more and more self-esteem."

The host referred to clips from Trump's pre-midterms rally in North Dakota, where he claimed he was the Goat (greatest of all time), ahead of Washington and Lincoln.

"It's so sad. He might be the most insecure person in the history of the world," Kimmel laughed. "Remember when we all used to hate people who talked like that?

"I'm starting to understand why Trump likes going on these roadtrips," he continued. "It's not only a boost to his ego; it's a chance for his number one fan and poster girl, Natalie Harp , his human printer, to see him in action and to get her in on the adoration too."

Kimmel then played a clip of Trump bringing out Harp, Trump's young assistant, on stage to deliver a printout. "I kinda get the feeling he's sign anything she handed to him – executive order, lunch order, divorce papers, you name it," Kimmel laughed.

Trump then appeared to leer at Harp as she left the stage. "Let me tell you: if the Epstein files were a facial expression, that would be it," the host quipped. "I haven't seen him that much in love since the last time he met with Mamdani."

Later in his speech, Trump once again defended his war in Iran, but then suggested that Iran could bomb some US cities. "Let them take out Los Angeles, let them take out San Diego," he said to cheers.

The "joke" did not go down well with Kimmel. "He's talking about Iran bombing us, and I know he says a lot of crazy things, I know this is something we'll forget about by Thursday when he accidentally swallows a baby at a rally or whatever the hell he does next, but that's one of the craziest, most indefensible statements I have ever heard even this maniac make," he said. "Openly musing about Iran, a country we are currently at war with, taking out two American cities while his adoring fans cheer him on. But it's OK because we're liberals, we deserve to be bombed."

"Can someone please change this man's diaper already?" he continued. "I think that old nut has been sitting in his excrement for too long. He has the ranta-virus, and it needs to be treated medically.

"Now we have our own president wishing death to America," he added. "We already had a huge bomb here this weekend. It's called 'Digger,' OK?"

And on Late Night, Seth Meyers opened with Trump's claim on Truth Social that gas prices are high because blue states like California are closing refineries.

"Really? Are you sure it has nothing to do with you bombing Iran for six months?" the host wondered. "Blaming California for high gas prices is like burning down your favorite restaurant and then getting mad at the Grubhub guy."

Trump also posted that he would support a Senate bill that would extend daylight savings time year-round, writing "who wouldn't want more 'SUN' in the afternoon than in the morning?"

"Uh … Stephen Miller?" Meyers joked, referring to the president's hardline immigration adviser.

In other Trump news, the president made plans over the weekend to send $90 payments to roughly 20 million senior citizens to help with Medicare costs. "Wow, 90 dollars to spend on healthcare?" Meyers deadpanned. "He's like an old man who still thinks you can give a kid a quarter to go to the movies."

And former White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt announced her next step, as she's set to join Fox News next month. "Well, it makes sense," said Meyers. "She's got everything they're looking for … she's blond."

articles.title: The Surface Laptop Ultra finally has a release date — and a starting price of $2,599
articles.summary: Microsoft announced pricing and an October 16th release date for the Surface Laptop Ultra, its powerful Nvidia RTX Spark-equipped device.
articles.body: Months after revealing its Surface Laptop Ultra, Microsoft has announced that the Nvidia RTX Spark-equipped device will launch on October 16th. Pricing starts at $2,599 for the base configuration, featuring an 18-core CPU, 24GB of RAM, and 512GB of storage. The Surface Laptop Ultra ships with a 15-inch HDR touchscreen display with up to 2,000 nits of peak brightness, along with a larger trackpad that supports haptic feedback. The device uses Nvidia’s new RTX Spark chip, an Arm-based processor with up to 128GB of unified memory. Both Microsoft and Nvidia are positioning RTX Spark laptops at the very premium end of the laptop market, designed for high performance across creative software, gaming, and local AI tasks. It comes with a sleek aluminum chassis that looks a bit like the MacBook Pro, which this laptop is meant to compete with. The Surface Laptop Ultra comes with a variety of ports as well, including three USB-C ports, an HDMI port, a single USB-A port, a full-size SD card reader, and a 3.5mm headphone jack. It also uses a magnetic USB-C charging solution. The Surface Laptop Ultra is available in a variety of configurations, with the priciest $5,899.99 model including 128GB of RAM, a 20-core CPU, and 1TB of storage. It’s available to preorder starting today.

articles.title: How Microsoft built its MacBook Pro competitor
articles.summary: Inside the labs where Microsoft tortures laptops until they’re ready to ship.
articles.body: Before Microsoft releases a laptop to the public, it needs to put the device through its paces. That all happens inside a windowless, warehouse-like lab on the company’s Redmond, Washington, campus, where the team developing Surface devices programs robots to press their buttons thousands of times, pelts devices with radio waves from giant antennas, and builds contraptions that drop objects from increasingly daring heights to see whether the products can hold up. Its latest laptop, the product I’m here to see, really needs to hold up. The Surface Laptop Ultra isn’t just another high-end config of the Surface Laptop, it’s the debut platform for Nvidia’s RTX Spark — Nvidia’s entrance into the world of Arm-based PC chips, and a chance to blow expectations out of the water when it comes to what a Windows laptop is capable of. Microsoft’s last big laptop push — the Copilot Plus PC initiative from 2024, focused initially on Qualcomm chips — “was really aimed at MacBook Air,” says Brett Ostrum, corporate vice president of Surface at Microsoft. Microsoft also wanted to go head-to-head with the MacBook Pro, but existing chips weren’t capable enough. “We knew that was not going to reach MacBook Pro-level compute.” Around that time, Nvidia began privately showing off what its forthcoming chips could handle when it came to AI, and Microsoft jumped at the possibilities. “It literally made a ton of sense for us in terms of how to go and compete with the MacBook Pro,” Ostrum says. “Nvidia was a logical choice.” The two companies have spent the years since working hand in hand, resulting in today’s launch. [Image: [Image: Much like the MacBook Pro, the Surface Laptop Ultra is a high-end device. It has a CNC-machined aluminum body, a huge trackpad, chicklet keys, and fan vents tucked underneath its slightly elevated base. There’s an array of ports, including HDMI and an SD card slot, and a high-res touchscreen that looks great up close. A model with 24GB of RAM starts at $2,599.99, and if you want the very top of the line with 128GB of memory, you’re looking at $5,899.99. Some of that price comes from the Ultra being one of the most polished laptops you can buy in the Windows world. But some of it comes from the all-new chip inside: the first of Nvidia’s RTX Spark line, which is supposed to bring essential components of Nvidia’s workstation-level power down to a portable device. The RTX Spark chips inside the Surface Laptop Ultra are geared toward local AI workloads and creative tasks. Microsoft says it’s powerful enough to handle compressed 280 billion-parameter AI models running locally — models that needed to run in the cloud only a year ago. The RTX Spark is both CPU and GPU, and the GPU should be able to handle Blender 3D objects with ease and cruise through other creator workloads in Premiere or Photoshop thanks to the system’s use of unified memory — the same approach Apple takes on its M-series chips. Microsoft is largely positioning the Ultra at developers who want a powerful GPU for local AI compute, but it’s also targeting the creatives and professionals who would buy a MacBook Pro. “It is built for us,” says Jit Hirani, lead designer for Surface devices. “We come to work to build a product for ourselves.” [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: Because Nvidia combined the CPU and GPU on the RTX Spark, Microsoft was able to make its Surface Laptop Ultra motherboard smaller and increase the size of the fans on the device. The space inside the machine is maximized for battery, with components neatly arranged in a black grid. Microsoft has also focused on repairability, with no components glued down and clearly marked instructions and QR codes throughout for disassembly. As this is an Nvidia laptop, you can also use it for gaming, but I get the sense that Microsoft is treading carefully about positioning this as a gaming laptop. The RTX Spark is an Arm chip, which means most games aren’t native and will have to be emulated. Still, I got a chance to briefly play an emulated version of Gears of War: E-Day on the Surface Laptop Ultra, and it ran buttery smooth, even transitioning between the laptop being plugged in and running off battery without a performance hit. [Image: The Surface Laptop Ultra has the world’s first built-in magnetic USB-C charging on a laptop. Microsoft put a lot of care into making sure the Ultra’s design was as premium as a MacBook’s, too. One detail in particular stood out to me: the way Microsoft has cleverly reworked its magnetic Surface Connect charging port. “I think we gave our engineering team probably about 300 iterations on this journey because it’s the world’s first built-in magnetic connect for USB-C,” says Hirani. “The single constraint from day one when we designed the product was that we could not change the universal USB-C [port].” Instead of losing a USB-C port to some custom solution, Microsoft has built a magnetic attach around the USB-C port instead. It feels very similar to the original Surface Connect, complete with a charging light and no need to precisely guide it into place. You can even disconnect the cable from the 140-watt charging block, reverse it, plug it back in, and use the regular USB-C port on the other end to charge all of your other devices. Ostrum tells me that Microsoft spent years “grinding on this” to make a magnetic USB-C charging solution, so my question to him is: Will we see this on more Surface devices? “We’ll wait and see,” he says. “We have been super passionate about that experience. This is the place where we wanted to introduce it to the world.” The amount of testing and product iteration that went into getting this charging port right is mirrored in the rest of the Surface Laptop Ultra. Microsoft has an Automated Experience Lab (AXL) tool that helps the teams measure the responsiveness of a device, beyond just regular benchmarks. That’s anything from measuring how long it takes to launch Microsoft Teams to how fast it is to type letters on a keyboard. [Image: The “BB8” robot that tests the Surface Laptop Ultra. This is all automated through an Arduino board that can inject code onto a system and measure its response times. Microsoft has created what it affectionately calls its own BB8, a robot that helps the thousands of engineers working on getting the stability just right for the RTX Spark platform. “We have engineers at Nvidia that are working on power, performance, graphics, stability, and Wi-Fi,” explains Ostrum. “When they work on each of those things, they have to complete their code, check it into Nvidia. Once Nvidia is satisfied with the stability and the performance of that chunk of code, it flows into the next branch.” That process creates a lag, sometimes lasting weeks, between Nvidia, Surface, and Windows all getting code ready for a new platform like RTX Spark. To speed things up, Microsoft has got Nvidia engineers uploading code remotely to this tiny robot that automates tasks that regular consumers do with a laptop. The miniature robot can unplug USB-C devices, use the touchscreen, pen, and trackpad, and open and close the device. [Media: “By allowing our silicon partners to download onto this setup, we greatly accelerate [testing],” explains Ostrum. “It might have been weeks from the time they were done with their code to the time they were ready to drop it to us. They can have that data back the next day.” Microsoft’s lessons of building Surface hardware for nearly 15 years have also been applied to the Surface Laptop Ultra in ways I’ve never heard about before. I’ve seen some of Microsoft’s hardware labs over the past 15 years, but the one I visited this week was eye-opening. It’s so secretive that I wasn’t able to take photos of the outside of the building or the lobby, and it lacks windows so nobody can see inside. It houses the unsung heroes of Microsoft’s Surface team who spend hours creating new ways to stress test new Surface devices. That includes simple tests like automated drop tests or rows of robots opening and closing laptop lids thousands of times, but it also includes electromagnetic compatibility and RF compliance testing, and X-ray machines and specialist electron microscopy equipment that are used to find failures at nanometer scale. [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: Microsoft also has what it calls a “CSI lab” to perform analysis on hardware failures and ensure the results are fed straight back into the manufacturing process. This can identify faults with component suppliers. In one case a few years ago Microsoft found touch failures on some of the displays it was using. The Surface team traced it back to sulfur and other halogens found on the display, after the supplier had changed the gloves that the manufacturing operators were using. The testing has helped Microsoft get to the point where it now has the confidence to take on the MacBook Pro. It also gets at the bigger reason Surface continues to exist inside Microsoft. Surface isn’t just a regular hardware business for Microsoft, it’s a way to show its OEM partners what Windows hardware should be capable of. Surface has helped push the industry forward on trackpads, displays, pen support, performance, and design. Without Microsoft’s own efforts, Windows laptops and tablets would have fallen even further behind Apple’s MacBooks. The Surface Laptop Ultra is the clearest example yet of that role. Microsoft is using its own hardware to prove that Windows can compete at the very highest end of the laptop market, while giving its OEM partners a target to beat. That makes Surface far more than a showcase for Microsoft’s software and hardware. It’s one of the ways Microsoft makes sure Windows itself keeps moving forward.

articles.title: Your phone says it's updated. Check other settings, too
articles.summary: iPhone, Google Pixel and Samsung Galaxy each handle security updates differently, and one screen saying "up to date" may not tell the whole story.
articles.body: Most of us have done it. A software update pops up when we're busy, so we swipe it away and figure we'll deal with it later. Then later turns into tomorrow, and suddenly that update has been sitting there much longer than we planned. There's another wrinkle. Even when your phone appears to be running the latest software, there may be another security update or protection worth checking. Apple, Google and Samsung all have ways to get security fixes onto your phone between larger software releases. However, they handle those protections differently. If you use an iPhone running iOS 27, a Google Pixel running Android 17 or a Samsung Galaxy running the latest software available for your model, there are a few places I would check right now. Join us for a free CyberGuy LIVE class. Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson shares practical ways to stay safer, smarter and more confident with technology. Explore classes on stopping spam, phone security, financial protection and using AI to get better healthcare. Each class is free, easy to follow and comes with a free printable checklist. See the classes and register at CyberGuyLive.com TURN ON LOST-PHONE SETTINGS BEFORE YOU NEED THEM Your iPhone can get security fixes between full updates Apple has a feature called Background Security Improvements that can deliver certain security protections without waiting for another complete iOS update. Apple says these lightweight releases can protect Safari, WebKit and other system libraries. That gives Apple another way to address certain vulnerabilities between larger software releases. iOS 27 is Apple's latest public iPhone software, so make sure your compatible iPhone is running it before checking the security setting below. How to check that your iPhone is running the latest iOS software If your iPhone says iOS 27 and no newer update appears, you're current at the time you check. How to turn on Background Security Improvements on iPhone Once your iPhone is updated: Your iPhone can then automatically install eligible Background Security Improvements as Apple releases them. These smaller protections do not replace regular iOS updates. You should still install full updates because they can contain additional security patches, bug fixes and broader changes throughout the operating system. HOW TO FIND COMPROMISED PASSWORDS ON IPHONE AND ANDROID Samsung Galaxy phones have their own update process Samsung Galaxy phones run Android, but Samsung adds its One UI software on top. Because of that, Galaxy owners often see different menus than Pixel owners. As of today, One UI 9 is Samsung's latest interface. Samsung began its U.S. rollout on Sept. 16 with the Galaxy S26 Ultra, S26+ and S26 after One UI 9 debuted on its newest foldable phones. However, you should not assume that every Galaxy phone eligible for One UI 9 has received it yet. Samsung rolls updates out by device, carrier and region. Whether your Galaxy has One UI 9 already or is still waiting for it, you can check directly from Settings. How to check for the latest Samsung Galaxy software On a current Galaxy phone: Depending on your Galaxy model or carrier, Samsung says you may instead see Download and install, System updates or Check for software updates. If an update appears, follow the on-screen instructions to install it. You can also check which version your phone is running by going to: That screen shows details about the software currently installed on your Galaxy. How to check the Google Play system update on Samsung Galaxy Galaxy phones also use Google's underlying system services, so there is one more update worth checking. If you have a Samsung Galaxy, you may be running the latest Samsung software available for your phone and still have a separate Google Play system update waiting to install. Google Pixel uses a different security update system Pixel owners will not find Apple's Background Security Improvements setting. Google handles the job differently. As of today, supported Pixel phones are running Android 17. Google began rolling out its September 2026 Pixel software update on Sept. 15, while the October 2026 Android Security Bulletin was published Oct. 5. Pixel phones receive regular Android software updates that can include security fixes. They also receive Google Play system updates, which let Google update certain parts of Android separately from a complete operating system release. That means Pixel owners should check two areas rather than assuming one update screen tells the whole story. How to check for the latest update on Google Pixel On a Pixel running Android 17: Google says supported Pixel devices running Android 17 are receiving the September 2026 software update in phases. Your exact availability can depend on the device and carrier. Pixel phones can also install downloaded Android updates in the background. However, you may need to restart the phone before the update becomes active. How to check the Google Play system update on Pixel You should check this separately: If an update is available, follow the prompts to install it. The Google Play system update can be easy to overlook because the name sounds like an update for the Play Store. It actually helps Google update underlying parts of Android and its system services. Don't assume automatic updates mean you're fully current I'm a fan of automatic updates because they remove one more thing you have to remember. Still, I wouldn't turn them on and completely forget about them. An update might need your phone to restart before the protection becomes active. Your device may also be waiting for Wi-Fi, sufficient battery power or the next stage of a phased rollout. That's why I like checking the update screens every so often. If you see an update waiting, finish it. A downloaded security fix cannot fully protect you if your phone still needs a restart before activating it. Older phones may eventually stop getting security fixes Your phone can keep working long after the manufacturer stops supporting it. That's where things can get tricky. If a phone no longer receives security updates, newly discovered vulnerabilities may remain unpatched. That can leave an otherwise usable device exposed to security problems that newer phones have already fixed. Apple supports iPhones with software and security updates for years, but older models eventually stop receiving the newest iOS releases. If you're wondering whether your current iPhone has reached that point, check out our guide on whether it's time to upgrade to a new iPhone at CyberGuy.com. Google currently provides seven years of operating system and security updates for Pixel 8 and newer phones, measured from when each device first became available in the U.S. Samsung also provides extended software support for many newer Galaxy devices, although the support period depends on the model. If your iPhone, Pixel or Samsung Galaxy no longer receives security updates, that should become part of the decision about when it's time to replace it. If you're thinking about upgrading your Pixel or Samsung Galaxy, take a look at our Top Android phones of 2026 for our current picks at cyberguy.com . Keep your phone protected beyond software updates Updates close known security holes, but criminals have plenty of other ways to go after your phone. Phishing texts can trick you into handing over passwords. Fake websites can imitate Apple, Google or a financial institution. Malicious apps can also create problems if you install software from an untrusted source. That's why I would combine current software with a strong device passcode, biometric protection and the theft-protection features available on your phone. I would also use a password manager to create and store strong, unique passwords for your accounts. Strong antivirus software can add another layer by helping detect malicious links, risky downloads and other threats before they cause trouble. Get my picks for the best 2026 antivirus protection winners for your Windows, Mac, Android and iOS devices at CyberGuy.com. Kurt's key takeaways I like security protections that can do some of the work for me. I'm not going to spend every morning checking whether Apple patched WebKit or whether Google released another system update, and I don't expect you to either. Still, seeing "up to date" on one screen does not always mean you've checked every security layer your phone uses. On my iPhone, I'd look at Background Security Improvements and Software Update. If you're carrying a Pixel, check both the Android update and Google Play system update. Galaxy owners should check Samsung's software update and Google's system update too. Then finish the job when your phone asks for a restart. That extra minute could be what finally activates the protection you thought was already there. Have you ever checked your phone's update screen and found a security update waiting that you didn't know about? Let us know by writing to us at CyberGuy.com. articles.title: Everything announced at Microsoft’s Surface Laptop Ultra event
articles.summary: Microsoft just wrapped up a big Windows and Surface-focused keynote in San Francisco, where it announced details about new Surface hardware and some updates coming to Windows.
articles.body: Microsoft just wrapped up a big Windows and Surface-focused keynote in San Francisco. The biggest announcement was arguably the release details about the Surface Laptop Ultra, its new laptop that’s powered by Nvidia’s RTX Spark Arm-based chip. The machine will start at $2,599 for a configuration with an 8-core CPU, 24GB of RAM, and 512GB of storage, and it will be released on October 16th. The laptop also has built-in magnetic USB-C charging instead of the proprietary Surface Connect magnetic charging port. The Verge’s Tom Warren published a deep dive all about the new laptop. Microsoft also announced that the Surface RTX Spark Dev Box, a mini PC for developers, is available for preorder for $5,999 ahead of shipping in November. In addition, Microsoft shared details about some updates coming to Windows, including “Hybrid Intelligence” features that lets Copilot use files on your Windows PC to take actions and a new search experience that lets you do quick actions from the search bar. You can catch up with all of our coverage from the event right here.

articles.title: Roku’s OLED TVs are up to $400 off during Prime Day, starting at $700
articles.summary: For Amazon’s October Prime Day, you can save a ton of cash on Roku’s Pro Series OLED TVs, which start at $699.99.
articles.body: Just over a week ago, we covered a deal at Amazon that knocked around 30 percent off Roku’s new (and first-ever) OLED TVs. The deal expired, but has returned for the final day of October Prime Day. The 55-inch Pro Series OLED is $699.99 at Amazon, which is 30 percent off its list price. The 65-inch model is $799.99, which is $400 off its list price, also at Amazon. Both models support a native 120Hz refresh rate, which is great for gaming, plus four HDMI 2.1 ports for 4K gaming at its full refresh rate, and support for Dolby Vision and HDR10 Plus. You’ll also get a backlit Roku remote control. There have been a few TV deals during Prime Day, though these are the lowest prices on OLEDs by a wide margin. We haven’t tested this model, but it’s an affordable way to get unbeatable contrast for your next movie or game night. [Product: Roku Pro Series OLED TVs

articles.title: Android’s physical navigation buttons are back on Googlebooks, but not the way you think
articles.summary: An oldie but a goodie — and kind of a necessity-die.
articles.body: A common misconception I’ve seen with Googlebooks is that the Quick Insert and Google logo keys are new. They’re not, as they first debuted a couple of years ago on some Chromebooks. But there is something new for Googlebooks that’s ripped straight from Android phones circa 2014. On every Googlebook keyboard, the F1, F2, and F3 keys are the old triangle, circle, and square navigation icons that first debuted on Android 5.0 Lollipop. These were the back, home, and app switcher buttons long before everything went to gesture-based navigation, and they’re still built into phones on Android 17 as an alternative. On Googlebook OS, these keys do what you expect: the left-pointing triangle goes back, the circle goes “home” by minimizing all open apps, and the square tiles your open apps like Mission Control on macOS / Task View on Windows. [Image: If I stare at these keys long enough, I can pretend I’m holding my old Nexus 6. It’s useful to have these buttons, and to have them matched across all Googlebooks. The back button seems sometimes necessary when using Android apps that aren’t really optimized for a desktop interface or mouse controls. I just wish a second press of the home button brought all your apps back to where they were, but that’s another feature called desktop peeking that uses a different keyboard shortcut. If you’re an Android nerd of yore, it’s kind of fun to see these buttons live on. But they’re also a reminder that you sometimes need a fallback when Android gets all Android on you.

articles.title: Teenage Engineering’s CEO says it’ll stop making synths
articles.summary: The end could be nigh for Teenage Engineering’s iconic OP-1 according to a Highsnobiety interview.
articles.body: Teenage Engineering founder and CEO Jesper Kouthoofd told Highsnobiety that it plans to stop making synths. And yes, that includes the iconic OP-1, which put the company on the map. TE isn’t just a music gear maker; it’s also a sought-after design firm. It’s collaborated with Ikea, Nothing, and Playdate, among others. But almost everything the company makes itself — the OP-1, the OP-XY, EP-133, TP-7, et cetera — is music or audio-focused. Which makes the supposed decision to abandon the market all the more confusing. Here’s the relevant quote from Highsnobiety: > Kouthoofd tells me that, as part of a reorganization last fall, he announced to his team he is planning to stop making synthesizers altogether. The OP-1 is no exception. Launched in 2011, it put Teenage Engineering on the map and has been central to its success ever since. > “Everyone was like, ‘What are you talking about?’ But I’ve come to the conclusion that, for us, the products aren’t the business,” Kouthoofd says. “We can be so much more than that.” Teenage Engineering did not immediately return a request for comment.

articles.title: Amazon lança tablets com Android pela 1ª vez e aumenta preços | G1
articles.standfirst: Aparelhos abandonam o sistema próprio da empresa e apostam em recursos mais avançados, como a Alexa+. Modelo mais caro custa US$ 550.
articles.summary: Aparelhos abandonam o sistema próprio da empresa e apostam em recursos mais avançados, como a Alexa+. Modelo mais caro custa US$ 550.
articles.body:
Logo da Alexa+ é exibido em uma tela durante evento de lançamento de dispositivos da Amazon, em Nova York, nos Estados Unidos, em 26 de fevereiro de 2025. — Foto: REUTERS/Brendan McDermid/Arquivo

A Amazon apresentou nesta quinta-feira (08) uma nova linha de tablets que, pela primeira vez, contam com a assistente de voz Alexa+ e utilizam o sistema operacional Android , do Google.

A empresa aposta que os consumidores estarão dispostos a pagar mais por dispositivos premium após anos de foco em aparelhos mais baratos.

A companhia, com sede em Seattle, nos Estados Unidos, vinha desenvolvendo os novos tablets sob o codinome Kittyhawk.

A Reuters revelou com exclusividade no ano passado que a Amazon planejava substituir o sistema operacional próprio, o Fire OS, considerado mais limitado, após anos de reclamações de consumidores e desenvolvedores de aplicativos .

O Fire OS é baseado no Android, mas foi modificado pela empresa para funcionar como um sistema independente.

Chamada de Alexa Tablets, a linha terá diferentes versões, com preços entre US$ 230 (R$ 1.155) e US$ 500 (R$ 2.510) . São três modelos: Amazon Alexa Tablet 12 Pro, Amazon Alexa Tablet 11 e Amazon Alexa Tablet 8.

Todos os modelos têm estrutura de alumínio, uma mudança em relação ao acabamento de plástico dos tablets Fire.

Os novos aparelhos custarão até US$ 550 (R$ 2.761) , um aumento significativo em relação ao Fire HD 10, modelo mais recente e sofisticado da linha anterior da Amazon, que custava mais de US$ 180 (R$ 904) , embora a empresa frequentemente oferecesse descontos.

O modelo mais avançado, com 128 gigabytes de armazenamento, custa US$ 550 (R$ 2.761) — o mesmo preço de um tablet Galaxy da Samsung e US$ 100 (R$ 502) a mais que um iPad da Apple, que parte de US$ 450 (R$ 2.259).

Tablet Amazon Alexa 12 Pro: projetado para trabalhar tanto quanto para entreter — Foto: Divulgação/Reprodução Amazon

A reformulação faz parte de uma nova estratégia sob o comando de Panos Panay, chefe da divisão de dispositivos da Amazon. A empresa pretende se posicionar em um segmento mais sofisticado e se afastar dos aparelhos baratos que vendia pelo preço de custo ou próximo a ele.

A estratégia busca fidelizar clientes para o uso de serviços como Prime Video, Kindle, aplicativos de música e o próprio site de comércio eletrônico da Amazon.

O foco em preços baixos, porém, vinha acompanhado de algumas limitações, como qualidade de tela e duração da bateria inferiores às oferecidas por concorrentes como Apple e Samsung.

A Alexa+, versão mais avançada da assistente de voz da Amazon, terá papel de destaque nos novos dispositivos.

Equipada com inteligência artificial generativa, a ferramenta poderá realizar tarefas e responder a perguntas. Para utilizar a Alexa+ nos tablets, será necessário ter uma assinatura Prime ou do próprio serviço.

A Amazon está priorizando aparelhos mais caros em um momento de queda nas vendas mundiais de tablets.

As vendas recuaram 12% no segundo trimestre em relação ao mesmo período do ano anterior , para 33,6 milhões de unidades, segundo dados da IDC. Nos Estados Unidos, mercado particularmente afetado pela escassez de chips de memória, a queda foi de 32%.

A participação da Amazon no mercado mundial de tablets também diminuiu. A empresa respondeu por apenas 1,9% das vendas no segundo trimestre deste ano, ante 8% um ano antes, segundo a IDC. A Apple lidera o mercado, com 34%, seguida pela Samsung, com 17,5%.

Os preços dos novos tablets não incluem uma cobrança única para remover os anúncios exibidos na tela de bloqueio.

A exceção é o modelo mais caro da linha Alexa, que não exibe publicidade. Para os demais aparelhos, s erá necessário pagar US$ 20 (R$ 100) para retirar os anúncios , valor superior aos US$ 15 (R$ 75) cobrados anteriormente nos tablets com Fire OS, segundo um porta-voz.

A Amazon afirma que os anúncios ajudam os usuários a descobrir novos conteúdos de acordo com seus interesses e que a receita gerada contribui para financiar outras inovações da empresa.

Com a adoção do Android, os usuários dos novos tablets não ficarão limitados aos aplicativos disponíveis na loja própria da Amazon.

A plataforma era criticada por desenvolvedores, que precisavam criar uma terceira versão de seus aplicativos, além das versões oferecidas nas lojas Google Play e Apple.

A integração com a Alexa+, por sua vez, é uma das principais apostas da Amazon para diferenciar os novos tablets de seus concorrentes.

A empresa investiu bilhões de dólares na reformulação da Alexa para incorporar inteligência artificial generativa e ampliar sua capacidade de realizar tarefas em casas conectadas, fazer compras e acessar serviços de outras empresas, como Uber e Grubhub.

O serviço é gratuito para assinantes Prime, mas ainda não é lucrativo. Os tablets anteriores com Fire OS continuarão funcionando, segundo a porta-voz. Ela, no entanto, não informou se a Amazon pretende manter o suporte ao sistema operacional e à loja de aplicativos.

No início deste ano, a empresa encerrou o suporte a modelos antigos do Kindle. Na ocasião, citou os custos de manutenção do software como uma das razões para a decisão.

articles.title: Sub-Rs 20,000 smartphone market may be heading to a 'collapse' and reason is the 'most-loved and hated' technology right now
articles.summary: The cheap smartphone may not disappear, but it could become much harder to find.
articles.body: The cheap smartphone may not disappear, but it could become much harder to find. According to Counterpoint Research, smartphones priced below Rs 20,000 could shrink by around 40% by 2030. That would mean roughly 230 million fewer devices in the segment. The overall smartphone market, however, is expected to recover to its 2025 volume by 2030. So what is changing?Rising memory and chipset costs are putting pressure on the phones that operate on the smallest margins. At the same time, the AI data-centre boom is increasing demand for the same memory components used in smartphones. For buyers, especially in price-sensitive markets such as India, the result could be simple: pay more for a new phone, accept lower specifications or look at the refurbished market.Why are budget phones facing a bigger squeezeThe decline in cheap smartphones is not being caused by one component or one trend. Shubham Singh, Research Analyst at Counterpoint Research, told The Times of India that the sub-Rs 20,000 segment is facing a broader structural shift.“Rising memory, chipset and other component costs are putting greater pressure on entry-level smartphones, where margins are already thin and consumers are highly price sensitive,” Singh said.Budget phones have less room to absorb higher costs because manufacturers are already competing for buyers at very low price points. If component costs rise, brands have fewer options to protect both prices and specifications.They can raise the price. They can offer less memory or storage. Or they can absorb some of the additional cost themselves. None of those options is particularly attractive in a segment where buyers are highly price sensitive.How is the AI boom affecting sub-Rs 20,000 phones This is where the AI data-centre boom enters the picture. AI servers require large amounts of memory and storage, increasing demand for components such as DRAM and NAND. According to Singh, that stronger demand is tightening memory supply and has pushed memory prices up nearly fourfold, with prices expected to approach five times their earlier levels.“The AI data-centre boom is adding to this pressure, particularly through strong demand for DRAM and NAND, tightening memory supply and pushing memory prices up nearly fourfold, with prices expected to approach 5x soon,” Singh said.For smartphone makers, higher memory costs can eventually show up in the products consumers buy. A budget phone could become more expensive while offering similar specifications, or a phone at the same price could come with a lower memory configuration.That pressure is particularly important at the entry level, where even a relatively small increase in costs can make it harder for manufacturers to maintain the same price point.Could this make smartphones harder to afford in IndiaThe impact could extend beyond what phone buyers pay. Affordable smartphones are particularly important for people buying their first internet-connected device. If new budget phones become less accessible, first-time buyers in lower-income markets could have fewer options.Singh said the trend “could make smartphone adoption more challenging for first-time buyers in developing markets.” India could feel this pressure particularly strongly because of its large mass-market smartphone segment.Singh said brands with greater exposure to the sub-Rs 20,000 segment are likely to face the most pressure if the cost of RAM, storage and processors continues to rise.The decline in the sub-$200 smartphone segment reflects a broader structural shift in the market rather than a single factor. Rising memory, chipset and other component costs are putting greater pressure on entry-level smartphones, where margins are already thin and consumers are highly price sensitive. The AI data-centre boom is adding to this pressure, particularly through strong demand for DRAM and NAND, tightening memory supply and pushing memory prices up nearly fourfold, with prices expected to approach 5x soon. This is translating into higher smartphone prices or lower memory configurations, particularly in budget devices. At the same time, premiumization and longer replacement cycles are reducing demand for low-cost smartphones, as consumers either trade up, hold on to existing devices for longer or delay purchases. This could make smartphone adoption more challenging for first-time buyers in developing markets, while creating opportunities for refurbished and pre-owned devices that offer better specifications at lower prices. Globally, the refurbished smartphone market is expected to grow 14% YoY in 2026, while in India, we expect it to grow 16% YoY. Brands with greater exposure to the mass-market sub-INR 20,000 segment are likely to face the most pressure, as they have less room to absorb higher costs without raising prices or compromising specifications. However, financing, promotions, trade-ins and older-generation models can help cushion the affordability impact.That does not mean these phones will suddenly disappear from shops. Brands can still use financing, promotions, trade-ins and older-generation models to cushion the impact of higher component costs.But the equation could become tougher: maintaining the same price may mean making compromises elsewhere.Could refurbished phones become the new budget optionThere is one market that could benefit if new affordable smartphones become harder to buy: refurbished and pre-owned phones. A consumer looking for value may find that an older mid-range or premium smartphone offers better specifications than a new entry-level model at a similar price.Singh said the same shift could create opportunities for refurbished and pre-owned phones, which can offer better specifications at lower prices.Longer replacement cycles could also keep more older smartphones in circulation. Counterpoint expects the global refurbished smartphone market to grow 14% year-on-year in 2026. In India, the research firm expects the market to grow 16% year-on-year.That makes the refurbished market an important part of the smartphone story as new-device costs rise.So, will budget smartphones disappear?No, but the budget smartphone market could look very different by 2030. Counterpoint expects the overall smartphone market to recover to its 2025 volume, but the affordable segment is not expected to return to its previous position.“The smartphone market will recover in unit terms, but the affordable segment will not return to its previous standing,” Singh said.The budget phone isn't disappearing overnight. But if memory and chipset costs keep rising, the next phone that offers the best value may not be a new budget model at all. It could be an older, better-specced phone bought refurbished.That could be one of the unexpected effects of the AI boom: making high-end technology more powerful while making affordable smartphones harder to build.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Amazon unveils new Alexa tablets with Alexa+ and Google Play Store access | TechCrunch
articles.summary: The lineup includes three models: Amazon Alexa Tablet 12 Pro, Amazon Alexa Tablet 11, and Amazon Alexa Tablet 8.
articles.body:
Amazon on Thursday unveiled a new lineup of Alexa tablets that feature personalized intelligence from its Alexa+ AI assistant and full access to the Google Play Store. The lineup includes three models: Amazon Alexa Tablet 12 Pro, Amazon Alexa Tablet 11, and Amazon Alexa Tablet 8.

The tech giant says each tablet features an aluminum unibody design, high-resolution displays, and runs on Android. Plus, with access to the Google Play Store at launch, users will be able to download millions of apps, including YouTube, Netflix, Gmail, and more.

Until now, Amazon’s tablets have run Fire OS and ship with its own app store. With these new tablets, however, Amazon is taking a different approach to reach a wider audience. An Amazon spokesperson told TechCrunch that these are an all-new product line with new hardware and a new OS, rather than a rebrand of Fire Tablets.

The Amazon Alexa Tablet 12 Pro measures 6.5 mm thick and is engineered for “perfect balance,” Amazon explained in a press release. It houses a 12-inch, 280 PPI display, a 120Hz refresh rate, and a 3:2 aspect ratio for more usable screen space, which the company says is perfect for reading, watching, or working. It comes in two display options: a standard display and a Nanomatte display with anti-glare.

Amazon says the Alexa Tablet 12 Pro delivers nearly three times the processing performance and nine times the graphics performance of any tablet it has shipped before. The company says the tablet can easily handle everything from multi-window multitasking and graphics-intensive gaming to 4K streaming. It features Dolby Atmos speakers, Wi-Fi 6E, and 16 hours of video playback.

The company also announced the Alexa Tablet Pro Pen and Pro Keyboard, which Amazon says are designed to turn the Alexa Tablet 12 Pro into a full workstation.

The Alexa Tablet 12 Pro starts at $499.99, while the Nanomatte model starts at $549.99. The tablet comes in Graphite.

The new tablets are launching with built-in access to Alexa+. Users will be able to say “Alexa” or tap the “Ask Alexa” button to get answers to questions, control their smart home, and more. With On-Screen Intelligence, users will be able to ask Alexa to look at what’s on screen to receive contextual help. For example, while browsing a list of trails, users can ask Alexa, “Which of these hikes is best for me?”

The Alexa Tablet 11 is an 11-inch device with a 2.5K display at 276 pixels per inch, 90Hz smooth scrolling, and a 16:10 aspect ratio. The tech giant says it’s designed for streaming, gaming, reading, and browsing. It features 15 hours of video playback and dual Dolby Atmos speakers. It starts at $329.99 and comes in Graphite, Amethyst, and Matcha.

The Alexa Tablet 8 is the smallest and most portable of the three, featuring an 8.7-inch display and an all-aluminum design that weighs 329 grams. It’s designed to be held in one hand and carried anywhere for reading, browsing, and streaming on the go, Amazon says. It starts at $229.99 and comes in Graphite, Rosette, and Teal.

All of the new tablets are launching with a new Kindle reading experience. When users open the Kindle app, notifications are silenced, blue light is reduced, and battery life can last up to 20 hours.

The company also announced on Wednesday that it’s launching new Amazon Kids tablets, with 8.7-inch and 11-inch sizes available. Bundles include a tablet, a kid-proof case, and a year of Amazon Kids+, which provides access to thousands of kid-friendly books, games, videos, and apps in an ad-free environment.

There are separate versions for pre-K kids (ages 3+) and kids 6+, as younger kids get a soft bumper case in designs from franchises like Paw Patrol and Barbie, while older kids get a slim hard case with a built-in kickstand.

All three Amazon Alexa Tablets and the Amazon Kids Tablets will go on sale October 14, 2026, in the U.S., Mexico, and Canada. They’ll launch in the UK, Germany, France, Italy, and Spain on October 19, while the Amazon Kids Tablets will also be available in Japan starting October 14.

articles.title: Amazon’s Alexa Tablets are coming for the iPad
articles.summary: With access to Android apps, a new display tech, and lots of Alexa, Amazon hopes its new tablets can bring more people into its AI universe.
articles.body: Amazon is launching a new lineup of tablets that bear almost no resemblance to any tablet Amazon has ever launched before. They’re not even called Fire, the name Amazon has used for its tablets for the last 15 years. They’re called Alexa Tablets, and they’re designed to do two things: bring Alexa Plus to the center of your whole computing life, and be straight-up excellent tablets. The most important thing about these new tablets’ software? They run Android. Full, Google Play-supported, all-the-apps Android. There are plenty of preloaded Amazon apps, of course, and some built-in ways to quickly access Prime Video content or shop for basically anything anywhere at any time, but it’s finally offering a proper Android experience. Panos Panay, Amazon’s SVP in charge of all things hardware and Alexa, tells me that “Google Play was a necessity, end of story.” But Panay picked Android as the second most important thing about the Alexa Tablet. The first, he says, is the hardware. The Alexa Tablet is two and a half years in the making, Panay says, and he directed the team to start completely fresh in their tablet design. “Start from zero, don’t use any components we’ve ever used,” he says he told them. “Just ask, what is it? What is a great piece of hardware and what is it supposed to do?” [Image: The three flavors of Alexa Tablet. There are three devices in the Alexa Tablet lineup, all of which go on sale October 14th. The Tablet 8 has an 8.7-inch screen, starts at $229.99, and seems mostly designed for reading; the Tablet 11 has an 11-inch screen, starts at $329.99, and is more for watching stuff. They’re aimed squarely at the iPad Mini and base iPad, and seem nice enough. But the biggest device in the lineup, the one Panay really wants to tell me about, is the one he thinks really shows off what Amazon is doing here. It’s called the Alexa Tablet 12 Pro, and it starts at $499. It’s 6.5mm thick and weighs 550 grams — a little thicker and a little lighter than the latest 13-inch iPad Pro — and comes with either 8 or 16 gigs of RAM and either 128 or 256 gigs of storage. It runs a MediaTek Dimensity 8400 processor, a chip you might have found in a high-end phone a year or so ago. All these specs are… fine. Good enough to run an Android tablet, but nothing to write home about. The feature that really matters, Panay says, is the screen. Panay has this concept of the “one thing,” a single feature on a product that absolutely cannot be compromised on, no matter what. Make tradeoffs where you need to, he tells his team, but not on the one thing. “And the one thing on this product was, let’s go make the perfect screen.” That screen is a 12.5-inch, 2800 x 1840 display with a refresh rate up to 120Hz and 500 nits of brightness. Its 3:2 aspect ratio, Panay says, is perfect for running two Android apps side by side. And on the most expensive, $549 model Alexa Tablet, the screen comes with what Amazon calls a Nanomatte display. The company partnered with Corning to actually etch a unique texture into the glass itself that is meant to be richer, higher contrast, and less prone to glare than a typical display. The process sounds similar to Apple’s excellent nano-texture finishes, but Amazon seems to believe its method comes with even fewer tradeoffs in contrast and sharpness. I haven’t seen the device in person yet, but The Verge’s Terrence O’Brien has, and it sounds like it has a chance to be as good as advertised. [Image: Add the attachments, squint a little, and it’s an iPad Pro. The screen also adapts to what you’re doing on the tablet. If you launch the Kindle app, it turns off blue lights to make the reading experience warmer and more serene; if you start reading comics, it’ll render them extra glossy. Amazon understands well that tablets are primarily consumption devices — and the company is very happy to optimize for your time in Kindle and Prime Video. The Alexa Tablet isn’t just for watching and reading, though. Amazon also made a keyboard case and a stylus, and Panay says he hopes people will use it as a secondary or even primary computer. He also hopes you’ll use it to do Alexa things. Amazon has been working on the LLM-powered version of its assistant for the last few years, and believes Alexa Plus can be more than just a smart home assistant. (Our testing suggests… otherwise.) You’ll be able to ask Alexa about anything you see on the screen, and the chatbot will try to offer recommendations, find information, and, of course, try to sell you anything it can find on Amazon.com. On these devices, Alexa Plus appears to be nearly as pervasive as Gemini or Siri on other tablets, and that’s precisely the point. It has always made sense for Amazon to make tablets. But for so many years, the company that has seemed to be happy to simply make everything as cheap as possible in the hopes you’ll sign up for Prime and buy some stuff in the store. Trying to actually make great tablets seems new, and frankly a little surprising. But if it got the screen right, and made the right tradeoffs elsewhere, Amazon might finally have a proper iPad competitor.
